description:
The strategy doc says: "A dedicated `benchbox-results` repository remains
an optional future extraction if corpus size or contribution volume starts
to overwhelm the main repo. It is not a Phase 1 or early Phase 2
requirement."

Without an explicit checkpoint, this becomes a perpetually deferred
question that surfaces ad-hoc the first time someone gets annoyed about
repo size. The decision has real trade-offs (CI permissions, contributor
friction, SHA tracking across two repos, history rewrite risk) that
deserve a structured evaluation rather than a hot take.

This item creates the forcing function: a defined trigger condition, a
pre-written ADR template, and a lightweight evaluation procedure. When
the trigger fires, the evaluation produces a yes/no answer with rationale.
Until then, this TODO stays in planning as a marker that the decision is
intentional, not forgotten.

anti_patterns.dont: design the extracted-repo architecture in this TODO
anti_patterns.why: that's the work that follows the decision; designing it now anchors the decision.

anti_patterns.dont: pick triggers that require manual measurement
anti_patterns.why: they will be ignored; favor checks the metrics script can compute.
the trade-offs depend on numbers we don't have yet; this TODO is a forcing function, not a decision.

preserves.behavior: Existing `results-data/` location and structure on `published-results` branch.
The strategy doc's "extract only if churn justifies it" disposition - this TODO encodes the trigger, doesn't pre-decide the extraction.

verifications.description: Trigger doc exists with quantitative + qualitative conditions
ADR template exists with decision matrix scaffold

work_units.notes:
Pick 2-3 quantitative triggers (any one fires the evaluation):
  - `results-data/` exceeds 250MB in the main repo
  - Sustained 20+ community PRs/month (3 consecutive months)
  - Contributor-reported fork/clone times > 60 seconds on broadband
And 1-2 qualitative triggers:
  - A maintainer formally requests evaluation citing operational pain
  - Phase 3 design begins (extraction may be a precondition)
Document in `_project/analysis/results-data-extraction-trigger.md`.

Template `docs/development/adr/TEMPLATE-results-data-extraction.md`:
  - Context (repo size, PR volume at time of decision)
  - Options:
      A. Stay in monorepo (status quo)
      B. Extract to `joeharris76/benchbox-results` (or similar)
      C. Extract with selective sync (data repo + lightweight pointer
         in main repo)
  - For each option:
      - CI implications (workflows currently in main repo)
      - Contributor friction (one-repo vs two-repo PR flow)
      - Hash stability (SHAs change if history is rewritten on extract)
      - Cross-repo SHA tracking (does the explorer pin a data repo
         commit?)
      - Operational cost
  - Recommended decision matrix scoring template
  - Decision section (filled in at evaluation time, not now)
  - Rollback path: how to merge back into the monorepo if extraction
    proves wrong
Reference: `git filter-repo` for the extraction mechanic.
work_units.summary: Write the ADR template covering the trade-offs

work_units.notes:
Extend `scripts/phase2_metrics.py` (from `define-phase-3-promotion-metrics`)
with a final section that runs the quantitative checks from w1 and
prints a clear "EXTRACTION EVALUATION RECOMMENDED: <reason>" message
when triggered. This piggybacks on the existing quarterly review
cadence - no separate scheduling needed.
work_units.summary: Add a one-line check in the Phase 3 metrics script that flags trigger

work_units.notes:
Append to `_project/analysis/results-data-extraction-trigger.md`:
  Procedure when triggered:
    1. Open new TODO `evaluate-results-data-extraction-decision`
       (active, owner = current maintainer rotation).
    2. Copy the ADR template to `docs/development/adr/{date}-results-data-extraction.md`.
    3. Fill in current measurements, score the matrix, write the
       recommendation.
    4. Get review from at least one other maintainer.
    5. Commit decision; if "extract", file a follow-up implementation
       TODO with explicit migration plan including history-preservation
       strategy.
    6. Mark this checkpoint TODO Completed.
